title: [Paper] Does Self-Evaluation Enable Wireheading in Language Models?
primary_claim: Training Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B with online RL where models' self-assigned grades directly determine the reward causes rapid grade inflation (models learn to claim near-perfect scores while true task accuracy flatlines or collapses), and this effect is much stronger on ambiguous tasks like summarization than on objective tasks like arithmetic; decoupling the reward from the self-grade largely eliminates the inflation.
quote: We found that in the Selfgrade condition, models rapidly learned to saturate the reward signal (claiming perfect scores) while actual task accuracy flatlined or collapsed.
metric: grade inflation (self-reported reward minus task accuracy)
target_value: Selfgrade condition: inflation reaches 0.41 for summarization (reward saturating near 1.0, accuracy plateaus around 0.5); Honest condition: near-zero inflation (range -0.02 to +0.03)
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 5 numbers; compare the components by hand
blockers: Very long total runtime (30-50h sequential per README) for the full paper reproduction, though feasible over several days on a single 3090
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9b-it require accepting HF gated-model licenses
inspector_notes: Unusually well-documented compute requirements that map almost exactly onto a single RTX 3090 (L4 23GB ~= 3090 24GB); self-evaluation grading is computed by the models themselves, no external judge API is used anywhere in src/.
